diagnostic_evidence.quote: Now let us analyze the equality case. In terms of matrix $M$, it can be achieved only if $M$ is non-negative (but not positive).
which finalizes the proof of the equality criteria.

issues.failure_explanation: The proposition claims an iff equality criterion, but the entire equality-case analysis derives the clustered structure from the assumption that equality is attained (a necessary condition) and then stops. The converse - that a matrix with orthonormal columns whose rows form three groups of pairwise collinear vectors with squared magnitudes $\frac{1}{2n}+\frac{1}{2p}$ etc. actually attains $\max\sigma_2=1/\sqrt n$ - is never verified. This verification is nontrivial: from the closure relation $pW_1\hat w_1+qW_2\hat w_2+rW_3\hat w_3=0$ one must show every cross-group pair satisfies $(r_a,r_b)^2=(W_a-\frac1n)(W_b-\frac1n)$ (equivalently $M_{ab}=0$, giving $\lambda_2=1/n$), while same-group pairs give $\sigma_2=0$. The $n=3$ base case, dismissed as trivial, contains no such argument either, and the inductive step never proves the sufficiency direction at any size.

failure_location.quote: The corresponding equality is achieved if and only if the rows of the matrix are clustered into three non-empty groups of $p, \, q, \, r > 0$ pairwise collinear vectors

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the converse verification: given the clustered structure with the stated magnitudes and $A^TA=I$, use $\sum_k p_kW_k\hat w_k=0$ to compute cross-group inner products, conclude $\lambda_2=1/n$ for cross-group pairs and $\lambda_2=0$ within groups, hence $\max\sigma_2=1/\sqrt n$; handle $n=3$ similarly.
issues.overall_effect: The sufficiency half of the equality criteria of Proposition \ref{pr} - the paper's advertised contribution - and part 2 (the 'equality holds $\iff$' claim) of Corollary \ref{co} are unestablished.
issues.title: Equality criteria stated as 'if and only if' but only the necessity direction is proved
issues.why_classification: A genuinely missing, contained nontrivial argument (roughly half of the central claimed criterion), but no substantive claim, regime, or rate must be lost and no new global proof architecture is required, so it is more than minor yet not serious.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Applying the similar considerations to all pairs of $w$'s and taking into account (\ref{ws}), we get

issues.failure_explanation: The magnitudes are extracted by selecting two vectors of a block, using the off-diagonal entry $M_{uv}=\frac{2}{pn}$, and summing the pair inequalities $|u|+|v|\ge\frac1n+\frac1p$ over within-block pairs together with $\sum|w_i|=2$. For a block of size $p=1$ no two vectors can be selected, and the summation yields only the vacuous bound $|w_c|\le\frac{1}{2n}+\frac12$ (no lower bound). For a block of size $p=2$ the single pair pins only the sum $|u|+|v|=\frac1n+\frac12$ (and collinearity), not the individual values $|u|=|v|=\frac{1}{2n}+\frac14$. Only blocks of size $\ge 3$ are covered, yet singleton and doubleton groups are within the proposition's scope (e.g. group sizes $(n-2,1,1)$, or $n=3$ with three singleton groups).

failure_location.quote: Let us select from $w_1, \ldots, w_n$ two vectors corresponding to the first block of (\ref{blck}) and denote them by $u$ and $v$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the diagonal entries of the already-derived block form (\ref{blck}): for every index $c$ in a block of size $p$, $M_{cc}=\frac{2}{pn}$ while $M_{cc}=\frac4n|w_c|-\frac{2}{n^2}$, which gives $|w_c|=\frac{1}{2n}+\frac{1}{2p}$ directly for blocks of any size (within-block collinearity being vacuous for singletons and already derived otherwise).
issues.overall_effect: The necessity direction of the equality criteria of Proposition \ref{pr} (and hence of Corollary \ref{co}, part 2) is incomplete for extremal configurations containing groups of size 1 or 2.
issues.title: Final derivation of the extremal magnitudes fails for blocks of size one and two
issues.why_classification: A local, routine patch (read the diagonal of the block matrix instead of off-diagonal pairs) repairs the uncovered small-block degenerate cases; the method, conclusion, and advertised scope all survive unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Then the three $2 \times 2$ matrices composed of these vectors as rows have pairwise different first (and second) right-singular vectors.
By Lemma \ref{le} vector $(\pm 1, 0)^T$ can be a right-singular vector of at most one of these three submatrices.

issues.failure_explanation: In $\mathbb{R}^2$, three pairwise non-collinear vectors can have collinear pairwise sums: $a=(1,0)$, $b=(1,1)$, $c=(0,\tfrac12)$ satisfy $a+b=2(a+c)$. Every plane vector is a square, so take $v_1=(1,0)$, $v_2$ with $v_2^2=(1,1)$, $v_3=(\tfrac12,\tfrac12)$ (so $v_3^2=(0,\tfrac12)$): the lemma's hypothesis holds, and by the paper's own formula both matrices with rows $(v_1;v_2)$ and $(v_1;v_3)$ have $\tan 2\gamma=\tfrac12$ (numerator $1$ over denominator $2$, and $\tfrac12$ over $1$) with non-orthogonal rows, hence distinct singular values and literally the same first (and second) right-singular vector, since that vector is determined by the direction of $v_i^2+v_j^2$. The lemma's conclusion therefore fails. The lemma is then invoked in Case A to guarantee that at most one of the three extremal submatrices of $\hat C$ has $(\pm 1,0)^T$ as $\sigma_2$-right-singular vector, so the strictness of the inequality in Case A - and with it the exclusion of Case A from the equality analysis - is unfounded as written.

failure_location.quote: Since $v_1^2$, $v_2^2$ and $v_3^2$ are pairwise non-collinear, their sums $v_1^2 + v_2^2$, $v_1^2 + v_3^2$ and $v_2^2 + v_3^2$ are pairwise non-collinear too, which finalizes the proof of the lemma.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the lemma by a statement matching its actual use: for three rows taken from the three clusters of an extremal configuration, the squares satisfy the unique all-positive relation $\sum_k p_k w^{(k)}=0$, so no two of the sums $w^{(a)}+w^{(b)}$ can be positive multiples (a positive-multiple relation would force a negative coefficient in the unique relation), and non-collinear or oppositely oriented sums still yield distinct first/second right-singular vectors; this contained argument restores the Case A step.
issues.overall_effect: The strict-inequality step in Case A of the proof of Proposition \ref{pr} is unsound; consequently the necessity direction of the equality criteria of Proposition \ref{pr} and of Corollary \ref{co} rests on a false lemma (the results themselves remain true).
issues.title: Lemma \ref{le} is false: pairwise non-collinear squares do not imply pairwise non-collinear sums
issues.why_classification: The lemma is false as stated and cannot be preserved in its stated generality, so its own claim is lost and the proof step it supports needs a new, contained nontrivial lemma; however, the version needed downstream is provable locally and Proposition \ref{pr} and Corollary \ref{co} survive without new global architecture or substantive loss, so the least severe complete resolution is moderate.
